text: This slice holds the rule set and the proof of the match and evaluates nothing: rwb-payment evaluates package PAYMENT_MATCH in its own worker, writes one local decision record per match and per missed payment in its own transaction and publishes it on rwb.decision-record.v1, while rwb-decision answers the version in force, its row and its test cases, collects the records, appends them to the central hash-chained ledger of rwb_decision, serves the reads and runs JOB-14, and it writes no proceeds row, moves no plan state and reads no ACE view.
why: The Work Package places the slice in rwb-decision with DP-03 and DP-04, while DP-03 keeps a record write in the owning service's transaction and DP-04 keeps the evaluation in the owning service; only a two-half split satisfies both and no source fixes the boundary.
read: Work Package B2-P7-022 story line; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 and DP-04 and R5.4; RWB-E2-008 sections 4 and 12; RWB-P8-E2008-APP section 1; Temporal and Drools Design slide 16 notes through the P7 context pack.
confirm: Solution architect with the decision service owner and the payment service owner
impact: Medium: the money row stays with the service that owns it and the proof with the service that governs the rule, so a later move of either half changes one service and no business value.

text: The record consumed is rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, keyed by entryId and deduped on it, in consumer group rwb-decision.decision-recorded.v1, carrying the source service, the entry ID, the decision code, the rule ID, the rule version, the case ID, an inputs reference, the recommendation, the final call, the actions, the outcome and the decided time; a match carries decision code D5, a missed payment carries its own code from LOV-DECISION, and a record that names no rule version is refused with MSG-P3-027 and parked on the retry topic rather than defaulted; the input age limit of VR-P7-001-3 is read as a parameter whose key stays a placeholder; and the decision-log read defaults to page 0 and size 50.
why: The legacy story gives Java signatures and two monolith endpoints, TSD P7 lists the entry fields but not LOV-DECISION or the read defaults, and no source fixes the target event payload or the parameter key.
read: RWB-E2-008 sections 4, 11, 12 and 14; TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2 API-P7-006; FSD P7 v3 A2.3 and VR-P7-001-3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06, DP-07 and DP-11.
confirm: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-payment, rwb-access and rwb-case and the reference-data owner
impact: Medium: the payload and the codes become contract and reference data, so a later correction is a contract version or a reference row and no scenario changes.

text: The dry run of a version is a read-only operation that returns testResult (total, passed, failed, failed case IDs), the per-test-case expected and actual result and the recorded dry-run counts, and the two boundary cases of the legacy window live in the version's own rule_test_case set — PAY-90004 at 10 days before its due date expected MATCH on row EXACT, PAY-90005 at 11 days expected UNMATCHED — so a caller supplies no case and the answer is reproducible.
why: No source describes the dry-run answer of an existing version or whether a caller may pass its own cases, and this story needs the boundary proved without evaluating a live payment.

confirm: Solution architect with the rule registry owner
impact: Low: the boundary is proved from data either way, so a later change of the answer shape is one contract change and no business value.
